newsitem.title: SUDAN: Sudan arrests key southern opposition officials.
newsitem.headline: Sudan arrests key southern opposition officials.

text.p: Sudan has arrested four leading southern politicians just days after it rounded up dozens of opponents suspected of planning assassinations and sabotage acts in Khartoum, southern Sudanese sources said on Thursday.

They said that former central government minister Joseph Ukel, former regional minister Izaya Mabior and former parliamentarian Joshua Dau were arrested on Tuesday outside Dau's house in the Al-Amarat suburb of Khartoum.
Security forces also picked up on Monday Ezeikel Kodi, a businessman and a former regional minister in southern Sudan, as he left the law offices of ex-vice president Albert Alier.
All four are vociferous critics of the Islamist government of Sudanese President Omar Hassan al-Bashir and they have often complained that the state is not giving southern Sudanese their rights.
Rebels in the mostly Christian and animist south have been fighting for autonomy from the Khartoum government since 1983.

They joined northern opposition members last month to wage an armed offensive in the south and east which the rebels say is aimed at pressuring the state and sparking a popular uprising -- the way previous governments in Sudan have fallen.
Ghazi Salah el-Din, the head of the National Congress which is the only political system in Sudan, has also said that the government arrested last week dozens of suspected saboteurs.

Sudan's spiritual leader Hassan al-Turabi told Reuters last week that the state had arrested more than 15 members of the opposition Umma Party and Democratic Unionist Party because of their role in the rebel offensive.
It was not clear if both Turabi and Salah el-Din were referring to the same group of people.
